comments.author: Jolly-Rip5973
comments.body:
Ok dude...here is a lot of feedback. I played the whole game on medium one shot without dying once and finished the whole game in 24 minutes. 

1) game run great! It's very smooth. Graphics look polished. This is a pro...   
2) game is too easy. By about level 6 my ship was so OP that I killed every enemy without even having to really move.   
3) different weapons are definitely cool. Controls are bit too sensitive like ship needs to move a little bit slower.   
4) boss battles are a bit too generic. Each boss should be unique. Different destructible parts was a good addition but it needs to be even more extreme like blowing off whole sections of boss piece by piece.   
5) music is pretty good and good enough. Sounds mixing is poor. The audio effects (like missle file, lasers and explosions) need to be louder or the music softer.   
6) It was difficult for me to see certain enemy bullets when they were blue.   
7) game is over all very solid but poor replayability because there just isn't anything new to see stage to stage. 

Suggestions: 

1) first suggestion is make you stages look different with different themes. This shouldn't be hard to implement. Make some fighting in space, some fighting on different looking planets, some fighting flying along the surface of huge capital ships.   
2) Add world building and some type of story. Stages should progress as if completing missions in places in the galaxy.  Add a screen with a little mission briefing between stages, give each location a name.   
3) Add a character like a cute anime girl that's the pilot on top corner. She gets excited when she completes a mission and looks distressed when the shields go down. It just needs to be a little head of the pilot type of thing. A game that did this was "U.N. Squadron".   
4) To add difficulty and variety, make it so when the shit gets hit after losing shield, weapons are downgraded.   
5) Like "Raiden" you could have variable power ups the switch weapon systems or upgrade the existing on if you pick it up at the right time.   
6) if you really want to add world building you could have different enemy types with different themed levels but this would be more work than simply adding level themes.   
7) You could add different plane tops and character selections like "Aero Fighters".   
8) "U.N. Squadron" also had a weapons arms seller character between missions when purchased upgrades".   
9) You could make the pilot a male character and then have a female hander or dispatcher that occasionally pops up to give orders or feedback. She should be cute. Think "Shifty" from Nikke: Goddess of Victory. 

As a general rule you want each stage to look different and show the player something new. This incentivizes them to keep playing because they want to see what the next stage looks like. If you have some simple story they also want to playout the story to see the full story.

replies.body:
If nothing else, give each level a different theme would go along way even if you don't change the ships. 

All you have to do it generate the scrolling background to look like something completely different. 

All those old 80s and 90s video games were like that. Even nintendo games like mario and donkey kong, you were excited to see what the next level was.
